title: McMoneagle's CIA Mars remote viewing (Mars 1 Million BC)
summary: Jason Jorjani tells of McMoneagle's CIA Mars remote viewing (Mars 1 Million BC), about 1984 at Monroe Institute, Virginia; Mars, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

as_told.title: McMoneagle remote views Mars pyramids, JPL contacts send photos

plain: Remote viewing is the claimed practice of describing a far-off or hidden place using only the mind. A researcher and philosopher named Jason Jorjani, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says that in 1984 a remote viewer named Joseph McMoneagle, working at the Monroe Institute in Virginia, did a session for the CIA in which he viewed Mars. Jorjani links this to a document known as "Mars 1 Million BC." Michels, the host, mentions it himself on a later episode with a former Army remote viewer. He says McMoneagle was tasked with viewing Mars as it was a million years ago, though he gives no date and does not mention the CIA or the institute. They tell it because, if true, a US intelligence agency was trying to use the mind to look at ancient life or activity on another planet.
